Explicit computations reveal that a representative of the first Atiyah-Chern class is exact in the total Weil complex, with its primitive representing the modular class in Lie algebroid cohomology. In the case of action Lie algebroids, the leading-order Atiyah-Chern classes correspond to the equivariant Chern characters. Applications to BV theories show that the geometric deformations naturally generate Poisson sigma models. These results provide a coherent framework for deriving field theories from geometric deformations of $L_\infty$ algebras.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyi Cui

item.title: On the limit of simply connected manifolds with discrete isometric cocompact group actions
item.description: arXiv:2307.07658v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the fundamental group of the equivariant Gromov--Hausdorff limit space \[ (M_i, p_i, G_i) \xrightarrow{eGH} (Y, p, G), \] where $\{(M_i,p_i)\}_{i\in\mathbb N}$ is a sequence of complete, connected, and simply connected $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with $\mathrm{Ric}\ge -(n-1)$. Here $G_i\subset \mathrm{Iso}(M_i)$ is a discrete subgroup satisfying $\mathrm{diam}(M_i/G_i)\le D$ for some fixed constant $D>0$. Let $G_0$ denote the identity component of $G$. Then $G_0$ is a nilpotent Lie group. Let $T^k \subseteq G_0$ be the maximal torus. Our main result asserts that the quotient space $Y/T^k$ is simply connected. Moreover, the fundamental group $\pi_1(Y,p)$ is generated, up to conjugation, by loops contained in $T^k$-orbits. More precisely, each generator can be represented by a loop of the form \begin{equation*} \gamma = \alpha \cdot \beta \cdot \alpha^{-1}, \end{equation*} where $\alpha$ is a curve from $p$ to some point $y \in Y$, and $\beta$ is a loop based at $y$ that lies entirely in the $T^k$-orbit of $y$.
item.dc:creator: Jikang Wang

item.title: Rigidity of Five-dimensional Shrinking Gradient Ricci Solitons with Constant Scalar Curvature I
item.description: arXiv:2411.10712v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate five-dimensional shrinking gradient Ricci solion $(M^5, g,f)$ satisfying $Ric+\nabla^2f= \frac{1}{2} g$ with constant scalar curvature. Fern\'{a}ndez-L\'{o}pez and Garc\'\i a-R\'\i o \cite{FR16} proved that the possible values of scalar curvature are $\{0,1,\frac{3}{2}, 2, \frac{5}{2}\}$. If $R=0$, the soliton is isometric to $\mathbb{R}^5$; if $R=2$, the soliton is a finite quotient of ${N}^{4}\times\mathbb{R}$ \cite{FR16}, where ${N}^4$ is a four-dimensional Einstein manifold; if $R=\frac{5}{2}$, the soliton is Einstein \cite{Petersen-Wylie2}. The most difficult cases are $R=\frac{3}{2}$ or $R=1$. In \cite{Li-Ou-Qu-Wu} we proved that it is a finite quotient of $\mathbb{R}^3\times \mathbb{S}^2$ if $R=1$. In this paper, we prove that five-dimensional shrinking gradient Ricci soliton with $R=\frac{3}{2}$ is isometric to a finite quotient of $\mathbb{R}^2\times \mathbb{S}^3$.
item.dc:creator: Fengjiang Li, Jianyu Ou, Yuanyuan Qu, Guoqiang Wu

item.title: Non-collapsed RCD spaces with local bounded covering geometry
item.description: arXiv:2412.06131v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study non-collapsed $\mathrm{RCD}(-(N-1),N)$ spaces with locally bounded covering geometry. Our first main result generalizes Gromov's almost flat manifold theorem: if the universal cover is non-collapsing and the diameter is sufficiently small, then the space is bi-Holder homeomorphic to an infranilmanifold. In the smooth setting with $\mathrm{Ric} \ge -(N-1)$, this homeomorphism is actually a diffeomorphism. As an application of our arguments, we show that Gromov's almost flat manifold theorem extends to the $\mathrm{RCD}+\mathrm{CBA}$ setting. Our second main result generalizes Fukaya's fibration theorem. Suppose a sequence of non-collapsed $\mathrm{RCD}(-(N-1),N)$ spaces with locally bounded covering geometry converges in the pointed measured Gromov--Hausdorff sense to a smooth manifold of dimension $k < N$. We then construct a topological fiber bundle map from the RCD spaces to the limit manifold. The fibers are infranilmanifolds, and the structure group is affine. Finally, although there exist collapsing Ricci limit spaces with no topological manifold points, we prove that if the sequence additionally satisfies locally bounded covering geometry and the limit space has dimension $k$, then every $k$-regular point is a topological manifold point.
item.dc:creator: Jikang Wang

item.title: Conserved quantities of distinguished curves on conformal sphere
item.description: arXiv:2503.23442v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give conserved quantities of two generalizations of conformal circles on the conformal sphere. One generalization concerns curves carrying a distinguished parallel tractor along them, which can be used to construct the conserved quantities. The other is the class of curves satisfying the conformal Mercator equation, the conserved quantities of which are computed using Lagrangian formalism. The two generalizations are not disjoint, and our main result is the relation between their conserved quantities. Explicit examples are also presented.
item.dc:creator: Prim Plansangkate, Lenka Zalabov\'a

item.title: On steady and expanding Ricci solitons with asymptotic symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2505.20576v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a symmetry principle for asymptotically cylindrical steady gradient Ricci solitons and asymptotically conical expanding gradient Ricci solitons. Our symmetry principle bounds the loss of symmetry from the asymptotic link to the interior by the dimension of the weighted $L^2$ kernel of the stability operator. For homogeneous links, suitable kernel bounds imply that the soliton has an isometric action of cohomogeneity one. The results apply in particular to strictly linear stable solitons, require no curvature sign assumptions, and allow orbifold singular sets of codimension at least four. Applications include characterizations of Bryant solitons and global $U(m)$-symmetry results for solitons with quotient-Berger asymptotic links. In dimension four, we classify asymptotically $SU(2)/\Gamma$-cylindrical steady gradient Ricci solitons with trivial weighted kernel as finite quotients of Bryant or Appleton solitons. Under the same kernel condition, we also establish toric symmetry for asymptotically lens-cylindrical steady solitons.
item.dc:creator: Michael B. Law

item.title: Rigidity of Five-dimensional Shrinking Gradient Ricci Solitons with Constant Scalar Curvature II
item.description: arXiv:2506.00887v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate 5-dimensional shrinking gradient Ricci soliton $(M^5, g,f)$ satisfying $Ric+\nabla^2f= \frac{1}{2} g$ with constant scalar curvature. Fern\'{a}ndez-L\'{o}pez and Garc\'\i a-R\'\i o \cite{FR16} proved that the possible values of scalar curvature are $\{0,1,\frac{3}{2}, 2, \frac{5}{2}\}$. If $R=0$, the soliton is isometric to $\mathbb{R}^5$; if $R=2$, the soliton is a finite quotient of ${N}^{4}\times\mathbb{R}$ \cite{FR16}, where ${N}^4$ is a four-dimensional Einstein manifold; if $R=\frac{5}{2}$, the soliton is Einstein \cite{Petersen-Wylie2}. The most difficult cases are $R=\frac{3}{2}$ or $R=1$. In \cite{Li-Ou-Qu-Wu} we proved that it is a finite quotient of $\mathbb{R}^2\times \mathbb{S}^3$ if $R=\frac{3}{2}$. In this paper, we prove that every five-dimensional shrinking gradient Ricci soliton with $R=1$ is isometric to a finite quotient of $\mathbb{R}^3\times\mathbb{S}^2(\sqrt2)$. Thus every complete connected five-dimensional shrinking gradient Ricci soliton with constant scalar curvature is rigid, so Cao's conjecture holds in dimension five.
item.dc:creator: Fengjiang Li, Jianyu Ou, Yuanyuan Qu, Guoqiang Wu

item.title: Timelike conjugate points in Lorentzian length spaces
item.description: arXiv:2509.12855v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study notions of conjugate points along timelike geodesics in the synthetic setting of Lorentzian (pre-)length spaces, inspired by earlier work for metric spaces by Shankar--Sormani. After preliminary considerations on convergence of timelike and causal geodesics, we introduce and compare one-sided, symmetric, unreachable and ultimate conjugate points along timelike geodesics. We show that all such notions are compatible with the usual one in the smooth (strongly causal) spacetime setting. As applications, we prove a timelike Rauch comparison theorem, as well as a result closely related to the recently established Lorentzian Cartan--Hadamard theorem by Er\"{o}s--Gieger. In the appendix, we give a detailed treatment of the Fr\'{e}chet distance on the space of non-stopping curves up to reparametrization, a technical tool used throughout the paper.
item.dc:creator: James D. E. Grant, Michael Kunzinger, Argam Ohanyan, Yasmin Schinnerl, Roland Steinbauer

item.title: Almost paracontact metric Walker 3-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2509.21809v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On a Walker 3-manifold $(M,g)$, we construct and study almost paracontact metric structures $(\varphi ,\xi ,\eta ,g)$, only by means of coordinate functions of a unit space-like vector field $\xi $ and the metric $g$. Necessary and sufficient conditions are established for $M$, endowed with these structures, to belong to one of the classes of almost paracontact metric 3-manifolds, according to the classification of S. Zamkovoy and G. Nakova. We find some classes to which the studied manifolds do not belong. The almost paracontact metric structure on a Walker 3-manifold examined in \cite{GC2} is obtained here as a particular case. Special attention we pay to an $\eta $-Einstein manifold, whose $\xi $-sectional, $\varphi $-sectional and scalar curvatures are investigated. Some local and global examples are constructed throughout.
item.dc:creator: Cornelia-Livia Bejan, Galia Nakova

item.title: An upper bound on the growth of minimal graphs
item.description: arXiv:2604.19630v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Graphs of solutions to the minimal surface equation over simply connected domains with boundary values 0 can have at most exponential growth.
item.dc:creator: Allen Weitsman

item.title: On triviality and scalar curvature estimation of gradient h-almost Yamabe solitons
item.description: arXiv:2606.26113v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this study we have explored gradient $h$-almost Yamabe solitons on both compact and complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds. We have established several sufficient conditions for the triviality of such solitons with respect to integral inequalities involving the scalar curvature and the soliton function. In this regard, we have acquired scalar curvature estimation under certain $L^1$ and $L^2$ integrability conditions, and defined signal of the function $h$. Our results extend and refine former works on almost and $h$-almost Yamabe solitons, and characterize the geometric structures of generalized Yamabe solitons.
item.dc:creator: Absos Ali Shaikh, Ananya Tripathi

item.title: Critical-point-free energy for fractional-Toledo representations
item.description: arXiv:2608.15714v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $S_g$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\ge2$. For a reductive representation $\rho:\pi_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$, let $E_\rho$ be the energy function on Teichm\"uller space associated to equivariant harmonic maps into $\mathrm{CH}^2$. For every positive integer $d$ with $3\nmid d$, all sufficiently large $h$, and every $g>h$, we construct an irreducible reductive representation \[ \rho_{g,h,d}:\pi_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1) \] with \[ \tau(\rho_{g,h,d})=2h-2-\frac{2d}{3}\notin\mathbb Z, \qquad \mathrm{Crit}(E_{\rho_{g,h,d}})=\varnothing. \] Consequently, the associated branched-minimal-surface forgetful map is not surjective in these nonintegral Toledo components.
item.dc:creator: Rivu Bardhan, Anu Dhochak, Pradip Kumar

item.title: Bounded Harmonic Functions on Products with a Parabolic Factor
item.description: arXiv:2608.22942v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a connected complete parabolic Riemannian manifold and $N$ is a connected complete stochastically complete Riemannian manifold, then every bounded harmonic function on $M\times N$ is independent of the $M$-variable. Equivalently, pullback by the second projection induces an isometric isomorphism from the space of bounded harmonic functions on $N$ onto that on $M\times N$. In particular, the product of two parabolic manifolds has the bounded Liouville property, thereby answering Problem~16 of Grigor'yan's survey in the affirmative. The key analytic input is a total-variation memory-loss property of the heat kernel on a parabolic manifold. We establish this property by showing that the time-one heat kernel defines an aperiodic Harris recurrent transition kernel and then applying the row-merging theorem of Jamison and Orey.
item.dc:creator: Ruotong Jia

item.title: A Complex Structure on A Rational Homology Six-Sphere with Two-Torsion
item.description: arXiv:2609.11541v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a compact, smooth, simply connected complex threefold. Its second and third integral homology groups are cyclic of order two, and its remaining homology groups agree with those of the six-sphere.
item.dc:creator: Zichang Wang

item.title: Special Lagrangian cones in Deep Learning
item.description: arXiv:2609.20159v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a matrix generalization of the cone of Harvey and Lawson and prove that it is an exact special Lagrangian manifold. We further show that it belongs to a family of exact special Lagrangian manifolds that foliate the balanced manifold arising in deep learning.
item.dc:creator: Tejas Kotwal, Govind Menon

item.title: A Llarull type theorem on complete noncompact manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.20498v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $n\geq3$, $2\leq k\leq n-1$, and $m=n-k-1$. We prove that a complete, connected, noncompact, oriented manifold $(M^n,g)$ with scalar curvature $R_M\geq k(k-1)$ is isometric to $\mathbb{S}^k\times\mathbb{T}^m_\Lambda\times\mathbb{R}$ if it admits a smooth proper map of non-zero degree to $\mathbb{S}^k\times\mathbb{T}^m\times\mathbb{R}$ whose spherical component is 1-Lipschitz. We also establish a weighted scalar curvature obstruction at infinity for sphere-torus targets with a higher dimensional Euclidean factor under suitable control of the Euclidean component. These results hold in all dimensions without a spin assumption.
item.dc:creator: Guangrui Zhu

item.title: Strong Uniqueness for Instantaneously Complete Chern-Ricci Flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.08233v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study strong uniqueness for smooth instantaneously complete Chern-Ricci flows on noncompact complex manifolds. Under suitable reference metric and positivity assumptions, we establish strong uniqueness for initial Hermitian metrics which are K\"ahler outside a compact set. The initial metric may be incomplete, and no curvature bounds or metric equivalence assumptions are imposed on the evolving solutions. In particular, we obtain strong uniqueness from complete initial metrics in this class with bounded Chern-Ricci curvature. We also prove stationarity of flows from the Euclidean metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and uniqueness of the instantaneously complete flow from the Euclidean metric on the complex unit ball for all positive time. Finally, on complex surfaces, we show that a Ricci flow remaining Hermitian for a fixed complex structure is K\"ahler at all times if it is K\"ahler at one time, and derive a corresponding strong uniqueness result for Ricci flows in this class.
item.dc:creator: Shaochuang Huang, Zhuo Peng

item.title: A sharp pinching theorem for closed minimal Legendrian submanifolds in the unit sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.18536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $F:M^n\to\Sph^{2n+1}$ be a minimal Legendrian immersion of a connected closed manifold, where $n\ge3$, and let $B$ be its second fundamental form. We prove that if $|B|^2\le(n-1)(n+2)/n$, then, up to a unitary transformation, $F$ parametrizes a totally geodesic sphere or is a finite covering of the image of the minimal Calabi product of a point and a totally geodesic Legendrian sphere. This proves Conjecture 1 of Luo and Sun [Ann. Inst. H. Poincar\'e C Anal. Non Lin\'eaire 40 (2023), p. 548].
item.dc:creator: Yong Luo, Linlin Sun, Jiabin Yin

item.title: Complete gradient Yamabe solitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.21078v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, all complete gradient Yamabe solitons of dimension at least three are classified. More precisely, we show that complete steady gradient Yamabe solitons are either rotationally symmetric manifolds or scalar-flat manifolds. We also classify nontrivial complete shrinking and expanding gradient Yamabe solitons.
item.dc:creator: Shun Maeta

item.title: The $\lambda>0$ case for $\Delta u=\lambda-c e^u$ type equation on high dimensional spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.28520v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by prescribed Chern scalar curvature problems in complex geometry, we study the equation $\Delta_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}V+\lambda(e^V-1)=0$ with $\lambda>0$ on spheres. For $N\ge4$ and $\lambda>2(N-2)$ with $\lambda\ne2N$, we prove the existence of a nonconstant smooth solution that is axially symmetric and symmetric about the equator.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Li, Qiang Niu, Wubin Zhou

item.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.35651v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$. We also show that the energy index of every critical spherical catenoid in $\mathbb{H^3}$, that is, the index of the second variation of its energy, equals four; hence the inequality between the energy index and the spectral index conjectured by Medvedev for geodesic balls of $\mathbb{H^n}$ fails.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Dorofeev, Alexander Pigazzini

item.title: On cylindrical directions of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ derived from contact with spherical cylinders
item.description: arXiv:2611.01912v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with spherical cylinders $S^2(r) \times \mathbb{R}$. We introduce cylindrical directions of these surfaces, defined by the axes of spherical cylinders having degenerate contact with the surfaces, and show that these directions capture the ridge condition of projected regular surfaces under orthogonal projection along these directions.
item.dc:creator: Masaru Hasegawa

item.title: $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$- and $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-invariant multidifferential operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.08418v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the dimension of the space of $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant (n)-ary differential operators on weighted densities for arbitrary weights, including the singular cases in which the usual elimination procedure breaks down. The proof relies on the strong Lefschetz property established by Stanley \cite{s} and Watanabe \cite{w}. We also investigate the corresponding problem in the super case.
item.dc:creator: Wafa Mtaouaa

item.title: Foliated and compactly supported isotopies of tubular neighborhoods
item.description: arXiv:2208.05876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a foliation with a "singular" submanifold $\Sigma$ on a smooth manifold $A$ and $p:E \to \Sigma$ be a tubular neighborhood of $\Sigma$ in $A$. Under certain "scalability" assumptions on $\mathcal{F}$ near $\Sigma$, we prove that every leaf preserving diffeomorphism $h$ of $A$ is isotopic via a leaf preserving isotopy to a diffeomorphism which coincides with some vector bundle morphism of $E$ near $\Sigma$. This result is simultaneously a foliated, compactly supported and parametrized variant of a well known statement that every diffeomorphism $h$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin is isotopic to the linear isomorphism induced by its Jacobi matrix at $0$. Particular cases of such a "linearization theorem" allowed recently to compute homotopy types of leaf preserving diffeomorphism groups of polar Morse-Bott foliations on lens spaces and the twisted bundle $S^2\tilde{\times}S^1$. In general, that "linearization theorem" can be used to reduce the study of the homotopy type of the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ to an investigation of the following three groups (being independent in a certain sense): (a) diffeomorphism group of $\Sigma$, (b) the group of leaf preserving vector bundle isomorphisms of $E$, and (c) the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $A$ supported in $A\setminus \Sigma$, i.e. out of the "singularity" $\Sigma$.
item.dc:creator: Oleksandra Khokhliuk, Sergiy Maksymenko

item.title: The principle of relativity in classical nonholonomic mechanics and $G$-Chaplygin systems with affine time-dependent constraints
item.description: arXiv:2407.06231v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the principle of relativity in classical time-dependent nonholonomic Lagrangian mechanics from the perspective of moving global reference frames. We also introduce time-dependent $G$-Chaplygin systems with affine constraints, which are natural objects for the invariant formulation of nonholonomic systems with symmetries. As far as the author is aware, the Hamiltonization problem for time-dependent constraints has not yet been studied. As a first step in this direction, we consider a rolling without sliding of a balanced disc of radius $r$ over a vertical circle of a given variable radius $R(t)$. We modify the Chaplygin multiplier method and prove that the reduced system becomes Hamiltonian with respect to the new time.
item.dc:creator: Bozidar Jovanovic

item.title: Finite element form-valued forms: Construction
item.description: arXiv:2503.03243v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a finite element discretization of $\ell$-form-valued $k$-forms on triangulation in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ for general $k$, $\ell$ and $n$ and any polynomial degree. The construction generalizes finite element Whitney forms for the de~Rham complex and their higher-order and distributional versions, the Regge finite elements and the Christiansen--Regge elasticity complex, the TDNNS element for symmetric stress tensors, the MCS element for traceless matrix fields, the Hellan--Herrmann--Johnson (HHJ) elements for biharmonic equations, and discrete divdiv and Hessian complexes in [Hu, Lin, and Zhang, 2025]. The construction discretizes the Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) diagrams. Applications of the construction include discretization of strain and stress tensors in continuum mechanics and metric and curvature tensors in differential geometry in any dimension.
item.dc:creator: Kaibo Hu, Ting Lin

item.title: Statistical Inference for Rates of Change in Spatial Processes over Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2601.02305v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Statistical inference for spatial processes from partially realized or scattered data has seen voluminous developments in diverse areas ranging from environmental sciences to business and economics. Inference on the associated rates of change has seen some recent developments. The literature has been restricted to Euclidean domains, where inference is sought on directional derivatives, rates along a chosen direction of interest, at arbitrary locations. Inference for higher order rates, particularly directional curvature has also proved useful in these settings. Modern spatial data often arise from non-Euclidean domains. This manuscript particularly considers spatial processes defined over compact Riemannian manifolds. We develop a comprehensive inferential framework for spatial rates of change for such processes over vector fields. In doing so, we formalize smoothness of process realizations and construct differential processes -- the derivative and curvature processes. We derive conditions for kernels that ensure the existence of these processes and establish validity of the joint multivariate process consisting of the ``parent'' Gaussian process (GP) over the manifold and the associated differential processes. Predictive inference on these rates is devised conditioned on the realized process over the manifold. Manifolds arise as polyhedral meshes in practice. The success of our simulation experiments for assessing derivatives for processes observed over such meshes validate our theoretical findings. By enhancing our understanding of GPs on manifolds, this manuscript unlocks a variety of potential applications in machine learning and statistics where GPs have seen wide usage. We propose a fully model-based approach to inference on the differential processes arising from a spatial process from partially observed or realized data across scattered location on a manifold.
item.dc:creator: Didong Li, Aritra Halder, Sudipto Banerjee

item.title: Poisson cohomology of "book" Poisson structures
item.description: arXiv:2603.17277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute the Poisson cohomology of the linear Poisson structure dual to the n-dimensional "book" Lie algebra, defined by [e_0,e_i]=e_i, [e_i,e_j]=0, for i,j=1,...,n-1.
item.dc:creator: Henrique Bursztyn, Hudson Lima

item.title: Geometry-aware similarity metrics for neural representations on Riemannian and statistical manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2603.28764v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Similarity measures such as centred kernel alignment (CKA) or representational similarity analysis (RSA) are widely used to compare the representational geometries employed by different neural networks to solve the same task. Yet, because existing methods compare the extrinsic geometry of representations in state space, rather than their intrinsic geometry, they may fail to capture subtle yet crucial distinctions between fundamentally different computations. Here, we introduce metric similarity analysis (MSA), a novel method which leverages tools from Riemannian geometry to compare the intrinsic geometry of neural representations under the manifold hypothesis. We show that MSA can be used to (i) disentangle neural computations of deep networks in rich vs. lazy learning regimes, (ii) compare the dynamics of recurrent neural networks and state-space models, and (iii) investigate the statistical manifolds of diffusion models. Overall, we introduce a mathematically grounded and broadly applicable framework to understand the mechanisms behind neural computations by contrasting their intrinsic geometries.
item.dc:creator: N Alex Cayco-Gajic, Arthur Pellegrino

item.title: The $L^p$ spectrum of the Stokes operator on hyperbolic 3-space and exponential decay for the Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2605.22212v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the $L^p$ spectrum, $1<p<\infty$, of the Stokes operator $A=-\PP\LD$ on divergence-free vector fields of hyperbolic 3-space of curvature $-a^2$, where $\LD=\Delta_B+\Ric$ is the Ebin-Marsden deformation Laplacian and $\PP$ is the Leray projector. The spectrum is the parabolic region $a^2\{4+z^2:\ z\in\C,\ |\im z|\le|1-2/p|\}$. For $p>2$ every interior point is an eigenvalue, realized by an explicit family of divergence-free swirl fields which leave $L^p$ exactly at the boundary of the region. It follows that the Stokes semigroup on $\Lp$ has exponential type exactly $-\mu_p$ with $\mu_p=a^2\bigl(4-(1-2/p)^2\bigr)$. At $p=3$ this is $35a^2/9$, which lies strictly above the rates $26a^2/9$ and $10a^2/3$ that follow from pointwise domination by the scalar heat semigroup and from interpolation, and strictly below the $L^2$ gap $4a^2$. For the Navier-Stokes equations with small data in $L^3$, whose global solvability on $\HH^3$ is due to Pierfelice, the solutions decay in $L^3$ and in $L^6$ at every rate below $\mu\cdot35a^2/9$, where $\mu$ is the viscosity, and no faster rate holds for the linearized flow. The exponent $3$ is the usual scaling threshold. Curvature fixes the time scale of the decay and introduces no new threshold.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Wang, Samuel L. Braunstein

item.title: A Hadamard Formula for Equilibrium Envelopes under Parallel Deformation
item.description: arXiv:2607.17187v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(X,\omega_0)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $U\Subset X$ have $C^{3,1}$ uniformly strongly pseudoconvex boundary. Consider the signed parallel family $U_t=\{\rho<t\}$, where $\rho$ is a defining function agreeing near $\partial U$ with the signed distance, negative in $U$. Let $u_t$ be the equilibrium envelope with zero obstacle on $X\setminus U_t$, and write $\Sigma_t=\partial U_t$, with outward unit normal $\nu_t$. We prove that the normalized Monge--Amp\`ere energy $e(t)=E_{\omega_0}(u_t)$ belongs to $C^{1,1/2}([-\tau,\tau])$ for some $\tau>0$ and satisfies the Hadamard formula $$ e'(t)=\frac{1}{n+1}\int_{\Sigma_t}\left(-\partial_{\nu_t}u_t\right)^2 d\sigma_{\rho,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}, |t|<\tau. $$ Here $d\sigma_{\rho,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the interior outward Anzellotti trace of $$ \frac{1}{V} d^c\rho\wedge \sum_{p=0}^{n-1}(p+1) \omega_{u_t}^{p}\wedge\omega_0^{n-1-p}, V=\int_X\omega_0^n, \omega_{u_t}=\omega_0+dd^c u_t. $$ This measure is positive and uniformly comparable to the induced surface measure. The proof combines uniform $C^{1,1}$ estimates up to the boundary from the interior with $1/2$-H\"older stability of the normal derivatives under the normal-flow identifications. We identify the boundary part of the normalized Monge--Amp\`ere measure with the negative outward trace of a divergence-measure flux current. The one-sided weak-* limits of the mixed Bedford--Taylor boundary measures yield the weighted total flux appearing in the variation formula.
item.dc:creator: Ziyu Li

item.title: Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow
item.description: arXiv:2609.00501v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove uniqueness of finite-time geometric endpoints for the M\"obius-invariant Willmore flow in $\mathbb{S}^3$ under uniform quantitative nonumbilicity. The multiplicity-counting varifolds converge, without reparametrization or M\"obius renormalization, to a unique integral two-varifold. An intrinsic transport estimate gives quantitative total-variation convergence of the induced area measures on the fixed domain and bounded-Lipschitz Cauchy control of their pushforwards. Together with Allard compactness and rectifiability, this upgrades subsequential compactness to full-trajectory varifold convergence. The limit has generalized Euclidean mean curvature in $L^2$ with the natural endpoint lower-semicontinuity bound. For finite maximal trajectories with initial energy at most $8\pi$, Jakob's subsequential alternative becomes sequence independent: the limit is zero, or it has unit density and embedded Lipschitz support of genus zero or one. For Hopf-torus trajectories under the same energy bound, nonumbilicity is automatic and the anchored constant-speed profiles converge weakly in $W^{2,2}$ and strongly in $W^{1,2}$ and $C^{1,\alpha}$ for every $\alpha<\frac{1}{2}$. At infinite time, the same method yields a unique limit under an additional finite-dissipation-length condition.
item.dc:creator: Mohameden Ahmedou, Ruben Jakob

item.title: Shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08248v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe the shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces, through their global integrations and their homotopy Poisson algebras. We construct the adjoint symplectic groupoid of the surface explicitly, show that admissible curves integrate to embedded Lagrangian subgroupoids, which are 1-shifted Lagrangians, and characterize when their shifted intersections are clean. For a component of the degeneracy locus, a canonical Hamiltonian flow on its shifted self-intersection recovers the modular period. On the infinitesimal side, the homotopy Poisson algebra of a connected admissible curve not contained in the degeneracy locus is $L_\infty$-isomorphic to its underlying cochain complex, and its $L_\infty$-isomorphism class is determined by the total contact multiplicity. The brackets of arity at least two can be removed by a change of tubular neighbourhood exactly when all contacts are transverse. At tangential contacts, the binary bracket retains the modular vector field. We establish this distinction using a general characterization of the $L_\infty$-isomorphisms induced by changes of tubular neighbourhood, valid for arbitrary coisotropic submanifolds.
item.dc:creator: Yassine Ait Mohamed, Maxence Mayrand

item.title: Geometric folding and maximal asymptotic variance
item.description: arXiv:2611.09697v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2\le1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm
